companyDossiers.name: Motif Neurotech

origin.detail: Incorporated in 2022 to commercialize Rice research; Rice later explicitly identifies the Robinson laboratory as its origin.

labRoots.detail: Rice Robinson laboratory; collaborative circuit and clinical expertise accompanied translation.

precursor.detail: A miniature magnetoelectric film platform demonstrated electrical neural stimulation in awake rodents in 2020.

whatChanged.detail: The development path moves from a laboratory wireless stimulator to a programmable epidural device and a company pursuing therapeutic systems.

milestones.title: Magnetoelectric stimulation in rodents
milestones.detail: Rice reports a miniature magnetically powered electrical stimulator.

milestones.title: Company incorporation
milestones.detail: Rice lists Motif among startups incorporated that year.

milestones.title: DOT human feasibility report
milestones.detail: Temporary motor-cortex stimulation elicited movement; a separate pig study examined longer implantation.

milestones.title: BrainMesh research program
milestones.detail: Rice and Motif participate in a funded distributed skull-implant research program with additional partners.

limits: Motor responses in a feasibility procedure do not demonstrate antidepressant efficacy.
DOT is an epidural stimulator, not a NET intracortical recording probe.
Founder names are verified; the Rice magazine’s grouped affiliation wording is not used to assign every clinician a Rice faculty appointment.

companyDossiers.name: INBRAIN Neuroelectronics

origin.detail: ICN2 reports an ICN2–ICREA spinout created in 2019; the company’s own timeline labels foundation 2020.

labRoots.detail: ICN2 and ICREA are the stated spinout institutions; IMB-CNM/CSIC researchers and a wider public IP consortium contribute additional technology.

precursor.detail: Graphene transistor cortical arrays and readout circuitry provide access to electrical signals including very slow components.

whatChanged.detail: The company combines academic graphene interfaces with manufacturing, readout systems and intraoperative clinical validation.

milestones.title: Formation dates differ
milestones.detail: Institutional sources give 2019; the current corporate timeline gives 2020.

milestones.title: Public IP transfer agreement
milestones.detail: An exploitation and development agreement links six institutional co-owners to company translation.

milestones.title: First-in-human study begins
milestones.detail: Graphene electrodes enter an intraoperative Manchester-sponsored investigation.

milestones.title: Enrollment completion reported
milestones.detail: ICN2 reports completion of enrollment in that first-in-human study.

limits: Graphene transistors and graphene stimulation electrodes are related material approaches, not interchangeable device specifications.
No NET descent, mentor relationship, exclusivity, or established chronic therapeutic benefit is inferred.

companyDossiers.name: CorTec

origin.detail: Founded in September 2010 as a University of Freiburg spinout spanning biological, microengineering and hospital collaborators.

labRoots.detail: Freiburg biology, IMTEK biomedical microtechnology and the University Hospital are the institutionally documented roots.

precursor.detail: Early Brain Interchange work combined brain-activity measurement with electrical stimulation in an integrated platform.

whatChanged.detail: The academic interface program matured into an implanted bidirectional system tested for stroke rehabilitation; the same investigational hardware was later used for computer control.

milestones.title: University spinout founded
milestones.detail: CorTec is formed in Freiburg.

milestones.title: Early platform and funding report
milestones.detail: The Bernstein Center describes the recording/stimulation platform and university participants.

milestones.title: First Brain Interchange human implantation
milestones.detail: Company reports implantation at Harborview/UW in a stroke early-feasibility study.

milestones.title: Same implant used for computer control
milestones.detail: Company reports computer interaction in the initial participant using the implanted interface.

limits: The inspected evidence supports Rickert, Schüttler and Stieglitz; no Rüttgen origin or mentor link was verified.
Computer control and stroke rehabilitation are distinct endpoints.
The 2026 report is a company report from an early-feasibility context, not a controlled therapeutic result.

companyDossiers.name: Neurosoft Bioelectronics

origin.detail: An EPFL LSBI spinout documented by 2020; its team combines laboratory materials expertise with engineering and translational development.

labRoots.detail: Lacour’s LSBI supplies the soft-interface research origin; Wyss Geneva supports translation.

precursor.detail: Thin silicone membranes, patterned conductors and electrodes are designed to follow brain-surface geometry while accommodating surgical handling and imaging.

whatChanged.detail: The work expands from soft-array fabrication and minipig validation to surgical recording studies and separate minimally invasive deployment research.

milestones.title: EPFL spinout receives translational support
milestones.detail: Catalyze4Life funds the LSBI spinout.

milestones.title: Soft-interface preclinical integration
milestones.detail: EPFL describes MRI compatibility, surgical handling and minipig recordings with Clinatec.

milestones.title: Deployable electrode research
milestones.detail: An EPFL soft-robotic eversion array is tested in a minipig; Neurosoft is named for clinical transfer.

milestones.title: Intraoperative human recording report
milestones.detail: Neurosoft reports use of a 64-channel stretchable interface during epilepsy surgery in two initial participants.

limits: Exact incorporation date was not established from the inspected primary sources; “by 2020” is deliberate.
The 2023 deployable research array is not assumed identical to the 2025 intraoperative device.
The human report does not establish chronic tinnitus treatment efficacy or justify its marketing superlative.

companyDossiers.name: ONWARD Medical

origin.detail: Courtine and Bloch co-founded the predecessor in 2014 with other researchers. Its history also includes the 2019 GTX–NRT merger.

labRoots.detail: NeuroRestore at EPFL/CHUV is an ongoing research-translation source. NRT adds a distinct corporate and spinal-stimulation branch.

precursor.detail: Spinal stimulation seeks to recruit preserved spinal circuitry; brain–spine research adds brain-signal decoding to control stimulation.

whatChanged.detail: Commercial development spans spinal neuromodulation, while the 2024 CEA licence adds a separately developed implanted brain-signal technology for ARC-BCI.

milestones.title: Predecessor co-founded
milestones.detail: Courtine, Bloch and other researchers establish the predecessor described in ONWARD’s annual report.

milestones.title: GTX and NRT merger
milestones.detail: The combined company takes the GTX medical name, joining complementary spinal-stimulation programs.

milestones.title: Brain–spine interface publication
milestones.detail: A digital bridge between cortical signals and spinal stimulation supports walking in one participant.

milestones.title: WIMAGINE exclusive licence announced
milestones.detail: ONWARD obtains rights from CEA for an ARC-BCI development branch.
milestones.dateBasis: release date; CEA page published October 17

limits: Courtine and Bloch are verified co-founders, not an asserted complete list.
The 2023 study is a research system; it is not labelled here as proof that all implanted hardware was an ONWARD commercial product.
NeuroRestore and CEA/Clinatec are separate contributors. The clinical paper does not establish generalized recovery for every spinal-cord injury.

companyDossiers.name: Corticale

origin.detail: IIT announced Corticale in August 2021 as a startup from Berdondini’s Microtechnology for Neuroelectronics team.

labRoots.detail: IIT’s Microtechnology for Neuroelectronics team developed the SiNAPS active-pixel recording architecture.

precursor.detail: SiNAPS integrates a small amplification front end under each electrode-pixel. The original paper demonstrated a fabricated 512-pixel single shank; its broader architecture supported scaling.

whatChanged.detail: The research ASIC architecture becomes a supported probe/headstage/acquisition/software ecosystem; later multishank research expands simultaneous spatial coverage.

milestones.title: Original SiNAPS paper
milestones.detail: Online publication precedes the 2019 issue; the demonstrated single-shank probe has 512 electrode-pixels.

milestones.title: IIT startup announcement
milestones.detail: IIT announces the four-founder company and its research commercialization plan.

milestones.title: Eight-shank SiNAPS paper
milestones.detail: The paper demonstrates recording from all 1,024 electrodes at 20 kHz per channel in behaving mice.

milestones.title: Corti-Q ecosystem documented
milestones.detail: The undated company page lists acquisition, visualization and analysis tools supporting SiNAPS.

limits: The original paper’s fabricated 512-pixel example must not be relabelled a demonstrated 1,024-channel implant.
The 2025 1,024-channel result is a mouse research platform, not human clinical availability.
Shared CMOS fabrication with Neuropixels does not establish historical descent.
